title: Minimax Risk for Mixed Average Treatment Effects on the Treated with Few Treated Queries
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Latest math referee pass; known one-dimensional common-uniform design caps novelty at subfield.
gap_reasons: The delivered frontier concerns a one-dimensional, known common-uniform design with public smoothness; the observational bridge preserves these restrictions and does not cover covariate imbalance. The conditional-length theorem matches the order in n, m, and s for fixed L, while sharp dependence on varying L remains unsettled; local efficiency is established above the transition at strict-interior regressions. Empirical retargeting and modulus inference come from [Hirshberg–Maleki–Zubizarreta](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1901.10296) and [Armstrong–Kolesár](https://www.princeton.edu/~mkolesar/papers/cate.pdf), so the contribution is the evaluated Bernoulli frontiers and all-procedure converses. Kennedy's [2024 conference abstract](https://ww2.amstat.org/meetings/jsm/2024/onlineprogram/abstract.cfm?sid=1161&tid=1161-p5) supplies no theorem text establishing duplication. The TL;DR and concluding scope sections are stale: they describe local efficiency, the matching conditional upper frontier, and supplied converse arguments as open or unverified despite their written proofs. The projected score reflects the benchmark's restricted reach and inherited methodology; routine rewriting can reconcile the contradictory scope statements but cannot establish applicability to the cited clinical design. proof_attempt_summary: Derived the all-procedure rare-treated MATT risk and honest-length frontier in the known one-dimensional common-uniform design, together with conditional-honesty and above-transition local-efficiency results. The attempted unknown-common-G extension was rejected twice; citation repair proved Paley-Zygmund directly and reused the verified Causalean convolution theorem. Latest math review passed, but the projected score of 7.2 capped the package at subfield; no F-stage formalization was performed.
tldr: Mixed average treatment effects on the treated compare each realized \(Y_j(1)=V_j\) with its transported untreated conditional mean \(E[Y_j(0)\mid U_j,A_j^{\mathrm{tr}}=1]=f(U_j)\). This causal target leaves a random empirical query of the unknown control regression. With iid uniform treated queries independent of a uniform-design Bernoulli--Holder control sample and arbitrary observable binary treated outcomes, the project seeks matching all-procedure root mean squared error and unconditional honest expected-length frontiers \(r_{n,m}=\{n^{-1}+d_n^2/m\}^{1/2}\), with a total split-control estimator, a finite-sample interval, and legal posterior-occupancy converses. The product-kernel submodel is exactly the iid observational MATT experiment conditional on arm counts under the displayed common-design and mean-transport conditions. Above \(m\asymp n^{1/(2s+1)}\), a cross-fitted control-score normal limit is derived; its moving-target local efficiency bound remains open. Conditioning coverage on all realized covariates creates an \(n^{-s}\) floor and a separate open fixed-design frontier. Exact translation by the observed treated mean makes the constructed errors, interval lengths, and coverage events invariant to the treated-outcome law, and both minimax values equal those of the reduced regression-query experiment.
gap: Yiu defines MATT and proves a regular fixed-positivity limit, Hirshberg, Maleki, and Zubizarreta give the empirical-retargeting construction, and Armstrong and Kolesar give fixed-design Gaussian modulus inference. None of those theorems evaluates an unconditional Bernoulli--Holder all-\(m\) MATT risk and honest-length frontier.
fill: The project combines an exact split-sample variance identity and a total histogram estimator with legal Bernoulli sign bumps, treated-query occupancy, and posterior-replica separation, then separates unconditional honesty, control-score asymptotics, and covariate-conditional honesty. An exact observable-translation reduction removes treated-outcome restrictions while preserving both all-procedure minimax criteria. A potential-outcome completion establishes the causal meaning for every observed law, and an exact arm-count bridge identifies the iid observational submodel to which the same frontier transfers.
